input: n is an integer with 0 <= n <= 15. Integers are plain int values, excluding bool. Containers are ordinary lists rather than subclasses; strings are ordinary str values. Standard built-ins are unmodified and no concurrent mutation occurs. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Declared size bounds do not guarantee allocation capacity or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The exact count of permutations of integers 1 through n for which each 1-based position i contains value v satisfying v divides i or i divides v. n = 0 returns 1 for the empty permutation. Permutations themselves are not materialized.
mutation_aliasing: There is no mutable input. The private used-value boolean array is restored after each recursive choice. No state is retained between calls.
numeric: Positions and candidate values are positive when modulo is evaluated, so there is no division by zero. Every recursive count and nonnegative accumulated prefix is at most n! <= 15! = 1307674368000, within the safe-integer range. At most n + 1 <= 16 recursive calls are live.
complexity: O(n*n! + 1) worst-case time and O(n + 1) auxiliary space. Each partial permutation scans at most n candidates; divisibility and used-value checks prune but are not assumed to reduce the factorial upper bound. Only scalar counts are returned.

helpers.name: count_from
helpers.contract: A position-based recursive closure. At position n+1 return one; otherwise choose an unused value satisfying either divisibility direction, mark it, recurse to the next position, add the count and unmark it.
